I'm investigating three things in this local-first markdown notes app (Tauri desktop + React Native mobile over a Rust core). Read AGENTS.md first for architecture context if needed, but focus your time on code, not the doc.

## Task 1: Transcription progress bar feasibility
Look at how transcription works: `crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs`, `whisper.rs`, and the desktop frontend `apps/desktop/src/features/recording/` and `apps/desktop/src/features/processing/` (queue hooks). Also check `apps/desktop/src/features/settings/` for how transcription status/settings are currently surfaced in Settings.
Answer: Is there any existing progress signal from the whisper transcription backend (e.g., percentage, chunk count, or just done/pending/processing/failed states)? Does faster-whisper (via whisper_env) provide any callback/progress hook we could tap, or is transcription a single opaque blocking call? What would be involved in exposing real progress (vs. a fake spinner) to the Settings UI?

## Task 2: Laggy switching between two recording notes in Feed
The user says: they have exactly two notes in Feed, both created from audio recordings, both already transcribed, and switching between them (selecting one then the other in the note list) feels "laggy" on desktop.
Investigate what happens when selecting/opening a note that has an associated audio recording — look at `apps/desktop/src/features/notes/editor/` (note-editor, use-note-editor, editor-context), `apps/desktop/src/features/recording/components/recording-note-header.tsx`, and how audio playback/recording note headers load data (e.g., does opening a note trigger an IPC call to read the full audio file into memory, or a redundant recordings queue snapshot poll, or something in `use-processing-queue`/`use-auto-queue-loop` that polls aggressively?). Check for obvious perf red flags: reading full audio blobs synchronously on note open, non-debounced heavy IPC calls firing on every selection change, recreating heavy objects/audio elements without cleanup, etc.
Answer with specific file:line references and a concrete hypothesis for what's causing perceived lag when switching between two audio-note selections.

## Task 3: Bulk audio file import feasibility (e.g. iPhone Voice Memos m4a files already on disk)
Look at how audio recording currently gets into the app: `save_audio_recording` command/service (search `crates/type-core` and `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs`), and the existing "import" feature (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/import/`, `apps/desktop/src/features/import/`) which imports Apple Notes exports — that may be a close analog for "pick file(s) from disk, create note(s)".
Answer: Is there already a code path that takes an arbitrary audio file path/blob (not from the browser recorder) and creates a note + queues it for transcription? What would adding a Settings-level "import existing audio file(s)" flow require — new Tauri command, frontend file picker, looping to reuse existing per-file note-creation logic? Note any existing single vs. multi-file picker patterns in the codebase (e.g. the Apple Notes import folder picker, or any existing multi-file dialog usage).

Report back concisely per task (a few sentences to a short paragraph each, with file:line refs), aimed at someone who will decide whether to scope these as actual dev tasks — not implement anything yet.

content.text:
## Task 1: Transcription progress bar feasibility

**No progress signal exists today — only a status enum.** The Rust side only tracks `RECORDING_STATUS_PENDING/QUEUED/PROCESSING/COMPLETED/FAILED` (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:411-416`, `RecordingQueueSnapshot` at `mod.rs:100-106`). `process_transcription_job` (`mod.rs:611-707`) just flips status to `PROCESSING` before the call and to `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` after — nothing in between.

**Transcription is a single opaque blocking call, not just at the Rust layer but at the Python layer too.** `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper.rs:117-168`) shells out via `Command::new(python).arg(&script_path)....output()` — `.output()` blocks until the child process exits and buffers all its stdout, so Rust literally cannot see anything until the whole transcript is ready. The embedded script itself (`whisper_scripts/transcribe.py:1-34`) also collects all segments into one `text_parts`/`words` list and does a single `json.dump` to stdout at the very end — no incremental flushing.

That said, `faster-whisper`'s `model.transcribe()` returns a **lazy generator of segments** (`transcribe.py:10-23` already iterates `for segment in segments`), and each segment carries `start`/`end` timestamps plus `info.duration` (total audio length) is known up front. So faster-whisper itself *does* decode incrementally — the opacity is a choice in how `transcribe.py` and the Rust caller consume it, not a hard limitation of the library.

**What real progress would require:**
- Rewrite `transcribe.py` to print one JSON line per segment as it's produced (e.g. `{"progress": seg.end/info.duration}`) instead of buffering everything into a final blob.
- Rewrite the Rust side to `spawn()` with a piped stdout and read it line-by-line as it arrives, instead of `.output()` (a real architecture change, since today it's a single blocking call inside the worker thread in `process_transcription_job`).
- Add a way to publish that percentage somewhere the frontend can read — likely a new field on `TranscriptionQueueState`/`RecordingQueueSnapshot` (`mod.rs:411-456`) updated from the streaming reader, polled the same way the UI already polls (`transcription-section.tsx:130-136` polls every 2500ms when `hasActiveWork`; `recording-note-header.tsx:82-85` polls every 6000ms). No Tauri events are used anywhere in this codebase for background work (import uses the same poll-a-global-snapshot pattern per AGENTS.md), so this fits the existing pattern rather than requiring a new IPC mechanism.
- A fake/estimated spinner (e.g. elapsed-time vs. a rough estimate from audio duration) would be much cheaper — no Python/Rust protocol changes — but would be inaccurate for variable transcription speed (CPU vs GPU, model size).

Net: exposing *real* percentage progress is a legitimate but non-trivial scope — it touches the Python script's output format and the Rust process-spawning strategy, not just UI. A duration-based fake progress bar is easy but a fake.

## Task 2: Laggy switching between two recording notes

**Root cause hypothesis: switching notes auto-loads the *entire* audio file over IPC every time, via an effect that isn't gated on user intent.**

`RecordingNoteHeader` (`apps/desktop/src/features/recording/components/recording-note-header.tsx:88-96`) has:
```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isRecording || !audioPath) return;
  if (activeAudioPath === audioPath && activeAudioSrc) return;
  void loadAudioPlayer();
}, [activeAudioPath, activeAudioSrc, audioPath, isRecording, loadAudioPlayer]);
```
This fires on every note selection (component remounts/re-renders per `notePath`). Since there's only one "active audio" slot in `RecordingsProvider` state (`recordings-context.tsx:61-62`), switching A→B→A means `activeAudioPath` never matches the newly-selected note's `audioPath`, so `loadAudioPlayer` → `playRecording` runs **on every single switch**, not just the first time.

`playRecording` (`apps/desktop/src/features/recording/hooks/recordings-context.tsx:111-130`) calls `api.readRecordingAudio(audioPath)` → Tauri command `read_recording_audio` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs:74-81`) → `RecordingsAdapter::read_audio` (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:379-394`), which does a synchronous `fs::read` of the **entire audio file** and base64-encodes it (`BASE64.encode(bytes)`, `mod.rs:392`) into one giant JSON string returned over IPC. The frontend then does `fromBase64` (`apps/desktop/src/shared/lib/notes.ts:19-26`), a manual per-character `atob`/`charCodeAt` loop — O(n) JS work proportional to file size — to rebuild a `Uint8Array`, wraps it in a `Blob`, and calls `URL.createObjectURL`, replacing (and revoking) the previous object URL.

So each note switch = one full-file disk read + base64 encode in Rust + a large string crossing the Tauri IPC boundary + a manual byte-by-byte base64 decode in JS + Blob/object-URL churn — for **both** notes, every time, even though nothing about the audio changed. For anything beyond a short recording (a few MB, which is easy for voice memos), this is a real, repeatable stall exactly matching "switching between two recording notes feels laggy."

**Secondary contributors (each individually minor, but compounding):**
- `RecordingNoteHeader` also independently kicks off `refreshRecordings()` immediately on every note switch and re-arms a 6s poll interval (`recording-note-header.tsx:77-86`) — an additional `list_recordings` IPC call that does a full recursive `collect_recording_notes` scan (`mod.rs:564-580`: walks the entire markdown tree and reads+parses front matter for every note) rather than being scoped to the current note. With only 2 notes this scan itself is cheap, but it's another redundant round trip fired per switch on top of the note's own `readNote` fetch in `use-note-editor.ts:102`.
- A separate always-on `useAutoQueueLoop` in `recordings-context.tsx:250-258` (`delayMs: 0`) runs `queueRecordingTranscriptions("auto")` immediately on mount and every 15s regardless of note selection, which also does a full note-tree scan — background noise, not switch-triggered, but worth knowing about if profiling shows periodic jank independent of clicks.

The single biggest, most fixable item is the audio-autoload effect in `recording-note-header.tsx:88-96` — it should probably require an explicit "Load player"/play click (the UI already has that affordance, but the effect makes it eager instead of lazy) and/or the backend should support streaming/ranged reads instead of one full base64 blob per switch.

## Task 3: Bulk audio file import feasibility

**No existing code path takes an arbitrary on-disk audio file and turns it into a note.** `save_audio_recording` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs:17-24` → `RecordingsAdapter::save`, `crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:241-280`) only accepts `audio_base64` (a `SaveRecordingArgs.audio_base64: String`, `mod.rs:46-52`) — i.e., bytes already in memory in the frontend (from the browser `MediaRecorder`, see `recordings-context.tsx:201-212` `handleRecordingReady` doing `blob.arrayBuffer()` → `toBase64`). It writes the file straight into `RECORDINGS_STORAGE_FOLDER` with a fresh UUID filename (`recording_audio_file_path`, `mod.rs:934-949`) and creates a note with `transcription_status = PENDING` (`mod.rs:265`), but note it does **not** itself enqueue transcription — the frontend calls `queueRecordingTranscriptions("auto")` separately afterward (`recordings-context.tsx:213-215`).

**The Apple Notes import (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/import.rs`) is a genuinely close analog**, but for a different medium (text, not binary audio):
- Its worker thread pattern (`run_apple_notes_import`, `import.rs:300-309`, spawned via `std::thread::spawn` in `ImportGateway::start`, `import.rs:73-88`) and pollable process-global progress snapshot (`AppleImportState`, `import.rs:134-152`, exposed via `apple_import_status`) are directly reusable for a multi-file audio import — same "no Tauri events, frontend polls" architecture already used by both recordings and handwriting queues.
- Its per-file loop (`import_inner`, `import.rs:311-352`, calling `import_one` per file at `import.rs:354-404`) is structurally what a bulk-audio importer needs: for each source file, allocate a note (`allocate_note_file_name`), write front matter, and (for audio) copy/read the file into `RECORDINGS_STORAGE_FOLDER` instead of parsing text.
- Its folder picker (`chooseAppleNotesFolder`, `apps/desktop/src/features/import/api/import-api.ts:41-51`) uses `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`'s `open({ directory: true, multiple: false, ... })`.

**Picker patterns found:** every existing `open(...)` call in the desktop app (`import-api.ts:46`, `whisper-engine-card.tsx:106`, `profile-section.tsx:44`) uses `multiple: false` — **there is no existing multi-file picker anywhere in the codebase**. The Tauri dialog plugin does support `multiple: true` (returning `string[]`), so this would be new but not exotic. There's also no `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs` usage in the frontend at all — the app currently always reads file bytes through Rust commands, not directly in JS.

**What a Settings-level "import existing audio files" flow would need:**
1. Frontend: a new picker call with `open({ multiple: true, filters: [{ name: "Audio", extensions: ["m4a","wav","mp3","aac","ogg","flac"] }] })` (new pattern, but a one-line change to an existing pattern).
2. Either (a) reuse `save_audio_recording` per selected file by reading each file's bytes and base64-encoding in the frontend (no new Rust code, but repeats the same base64-round-trip cost flagged in Task 2, now for potentially many/larger files — likely fine for occasional bulk import, unlike the "every note switch" case), or (b) add a new Tauri command (e.g. `import_audio_files(paths, folder_path)`) that does `fs::copy`/`fs::read`+`fs::write` directly server-side, avoiding base64 entirely — more scalable and more consistent with how the Apple import already avoids round-tripping file bytes through the frontend.
3. Loop over selected files creating one note per file (mirroring `import_one`'s allocate-name + front-matter + `update_order_append` shape, adapted for `RECORDING_FRONTMATTER_TYPE` metadata instead of plain text body), then a call to `queue_local_transcriptions` (or automatically enqueue each, matching the recorder's own `handleRecordingReady` flow at `recordings-context.tsx:213-215`) to get them transcribed.
4. Progress: since importing dozens of m4a files could take a while (mostly file I/O, cheap), either reuse the existing `RecordingQueueSnapshot`/`recordingsList` polling that Settings' Transcription section already displays, or add an `AppleImportState`-style dedicated snapshot if you want copy-progress separate from transcription-progress.

Overall this is a moderate, well-scoped feature: no fundamentally new architecture, but it does need one new Tauri command (or reuse with a loop), a new multi-file picker call (first of its kind here), and decisions about whether to route bytes through base64 (reuse) or add a path-based copy command (cleaner for bulk/large files).

No Tauri events are used anywhere in this codebase for background work (import uses the same poll-a-global-snapshot pattern per AGENTS.md), so this fits the existing pattern rather than requiring a new IPC mechanism.
- A fake/estimated spinner (e.g. elapsed-time vs. a rough estimate from audio duration) would be much cheaper — no Python/Rust protocol changes — but would be inaccurate for variable transcription speed (CPU vs GPU, model size).

Net: exposing *real* percentage progress is a legitimate but non-trivial scope — it touches the Python script's output format and the Rust process-spawning strategy, not just UI. A duration-based fake progress bar is easy but a fake.

## Task 2: Laggy switching between two recording notes

**Root cause hypothesis: switching notes auto-loads the *entire* audio file over IPC every time, via an effect that isn't gated on user intent.**

`RecordingNoteHeader` (`apps/desktop/src/features/recording/components/recording-note-header.tsx:88-96`) has:
```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isRecording || !audioPath) return;
  if (activeAudioPath === audioPath && activeAudioSrc) return;
  void loadAudioPlayer();
}, [activeAudioPath, activeAudioSrc, audioPath, isRecording, loadAudioPlayer]);
```
This fires on every note selection (component remounts/re-renders per `notePath`). Since there's only one "active audio" slot in `RecordingsProvider` state (`recordings-context.tsx:61-62`), switching A→B→A means `activeAudioPath` never matches the newly-selected note's `audioPath`, so `loadAudioPlayer` → `playRecording` runs **on every single switch**, not just the first time.

`playRecording` (`apps/desktop/src/features/recording/hooks/recordings-context.tsx:111-130`) calls `api.readRecordingAudio(audioPath)` → Tauri command `read_recording_audio` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs:74-81`) → `RecordingsAdapter::read_audio` (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:379-394`), which does a synchronous `fs::read` of the **entire audio file** and base64-encodes it (`BASE64.encode(bytes)`, `mod.rs:392`) into one giant JSON string returned over IPC. The frontend then does `fromBase64` (`apps/desktop/src/shared/lib/notes.ts:19-26`), a manual per-character `atob`/`charCodeAt` loop — O(n) JS work proportional to file size — to rebuild a `Uint8Array`, wraps it in a `Blob`, and calls `URL.createObjectURL`, replacing (and revoking) the previous object URL.

So each note switch = one full-file disk read + base64 encode in Rust + a large string crossing the Tauri IPC boundary + a manual byte-by-byte base64 decode in JS + Blob/object-URL churn — for **both** notes, every time, even though nothing about the audio changed. For anything beyond a short recording (a few MB, which is easy for voice memos), this is a real, repeatable stall exactly matching "switching between two recording notes feels laggy."

**Secondary contributors (each individually minor, but compounding):**
- `RecordingNoteHeader` also independently kicks off `refreshRecordings()` immediately on every note switch and re-arms a 6s poll interval (`recording-note-header.tsx:77-86`) — an additional `list_recordings` IPC call that does a full recursive `collect_recording_notes` scan (`mod.rs:564-580`: walks the entire markdown tree and reads+parses front matter for every note) rather than being scoped to the current note. With only 2 notes this scan itself is cheap, but it's another redundant round trip fired per switch on top of the note's own `readNote` fetch in `use-note-editor.ts:102`.
- A separate always-on `useAutoQueueLoop` in `recordings-context.tsx:250-258` (`delayMs: 0`) runs `queueRecordingTranscriptions("auto")` immediately on mount and every 15s regardless of note selection, which also does a full note-tree scan — background noise, not switch-triggered, but worth knowing about if profiling shows periodic jank independent of clicks.

The single biggest, most fixable item is the audio-autoload effect in `recording-note-header.tsx:88-96` — it should probably require an explicit "Load player"/play click (the UI already has that affordance, but the effect makes it eager instead of lazy) and/or the backend should support streaming/ranged reads instead of one full base64 blob per switch.

## Task 3: Bulk audio file import feasibility

**No existing code path takes an arbitrary on-disk audio file and turns it into a note.** `save_audio_recording` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs:17-24` → `RecordingsAdapter::save`, `crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:241-280`) only accepts `audio_base64` (a `SaveRecordingArgs.audio_base64: String`, `mod.rs:46-52`) — i.e., bytes already in memory in the frontend (from the browser `MediaRecorder`, see `recordings-context.tsx:201-212` `handleRecordingReady` doing `blob.arrayBuffer()` → `toBase64`). It writes the file straight into `RECORDINGS_STORAGE_FOLDER` with a fresh UUID filename (`recording_audio_file_path`, `mod.rs:934-949`) and creates a note with `transcription_status = PENDING` (`mod.rs:265`), but note it does **not** itself enqueue transcription — the frontend calls `queueRecordingTranscriptions("auto")` separately afterward (`recordings-context.tsx:213-215`).

**The Apple Notes import (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/import.rs`) is a genuinely close analog**, but for a different medium (text, not binary audio):
- Its worker thread pattern (`run_apple_notes_import`, `import.rs:300-309`, spawned via `std::thread::spawn` in `ImportGateway::start`, `import.rs:73-88`) and pollable process-global progress snapshot (`AppleImportState`, `import.rs:134-152`, exposed via `apple_import_status`) are directly reusable for a multi-file audio import — same "no Tauri events, frontend polls" architecture already used by both recordings and handwriting queues.
- Its per-file loop (`import_inner`, `import.rs:311-352`, calling `import_one` per file at `import.rs:354-404`) is structurally what a bulk-audio importer needs: for each source file, allocate a note (`allocate_note_file_name`), write front matter, and (for audio) copy/read the file into `RECORDINGS_STORAGE_FOLDER` instead of parsing text.
- Its folder picker (`chooseAppleNotesFolder`, `apps/desktop/src/features/import/api/import-api.ts:41-51`) uses `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`'s `open({ directory: true, multiple: false, ... })`.

**Picker patterns found:** every existing `open(...)` call in the desktop app (`import-api.ts:46`, `whisper-engine-card.tsx:106`, `profile-section.tsx:44`) uses `multiple: false` — **there is no existing multi-file picker anywhere in the codebase**. The Tauri dialog plugin does support `multiple: true` (returning `string[]`), so this would be new but not exotic. There's also no `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs` usage in the frontend at all — the app currently always reads file bytes through Rust commands, not directly in JS.

**What a Settings-level "import existing audio files" flow would need:**
1. Frontend: a new picker call with `open({ multiple: true, filters: [{ name: "Audio", extensions: ["m4a","wav","mp3","aac","ogg","flac"] }] })` (new pattern, but a one-line change to an existing pattern).
2. Either (a) reuse `save_audio_recording` per selected file by reading each file's bytes and base64-encoding in the frontend (no new Rust code, but repeats the same base64-round-trip cost flagged in Task 2, now for potentially many/larger files — likely fine for occasional bulk import, unlike the "every note switch" case), or (b) add a new Tauri command (e.g. `import_audio_files(paths, folder_path)`) that does `fs::copy`/`fs::read`+`fs::write` directly server-side, avoiding base64 entirely — more scalable and more consistent with how the Apple import already avoids round-tripping file bytes through the frontend.
3. Loop over selected files creating one note per file (mirroring `import_one`'s allocate-name + front-matter + `update_order_append` shape, adapted for `RECORDING_FRONTMATTER_TYPE` metadata instead of plain text body), then a call to `queue_local_transcriptions` (or automatically enqueue each, matching the recorder's own `handleRecordingReady` flow at `recordings-context.tsx:213-215`) to get them transcribed.
4. Progress: since importing dozens of m4a files could take a while (mostly file I/O, cheap), either reuse the existing `RecordingQueueSnapshot`/`recordingsList` polling that Settings' Transcription section already displays, or add an `AppleImportState`-style dedicated snapshot if you want copy-progress separate from transcription-progress.

Overall this is a moderate, well-scoped feature: no fundamentally new architecture, but it does need one new Tauri command (or reuse with a loop), a new multi-file picker call (first of its kind here), and decisions about whether to route bytes through base64 (reuse) or add a path-based copy command (cleaner for bulk/large files).

aiTitle: Улучшить транскрайб и загрузку аудио файлов

content.text:
Вот что нашёл по всем трём вопросам.

## 1. Прогресс-бар транскрайба

Сейчас реального прогресса нет — только статусы `pending/queued/processing/completed/failed`. Транскрайбция — это один блокирующий вызов Python-скрипта (`whisper.rs`), Rust ждёт `.output()` и видит результат только когда всё готово целиком. Сам faster-whisper внутри отдаёт сегменты лениво (по факту прогресс есть), но `transcribe.py` собирает всё в один JSON и пишет в конце — так что дорога наружу перекрыта архитектурно, а не библиотекой.

Настоящий процентный прогресс потребует: переписать `transcribe.py` чтобы стримить прогресс построчно, переписать Rust-сторону с `.output()` на `spawn()` + построчное чтение stdout, и завести новое поле в снэпшоте очереди, которое фронт уже умеет поллить (тут ничего нового придумывать не надо, механизм поллинга уже есть). Это реальная, но не тривиальная задача — трогает и Python, и Rust.

Дешёвая альтернатива — фейковый прогресс-бар на основе длительности аудио и примерной скорости модели (без изменений в протоколе), но он будет неточным при разной скорости (CPU vs GPU, размер модели).

## 2. Лаги при переключении между двумя записями

Нашёл конкретную причину. В `recording-note-header.tsx` есть эффект, который при **каждом** открытии заметки с аудио запускает `loadAudioPlayer()`, если "активный" путь к аудио не совпадает с текущим — а поскольку слот активного аудио один на всё приложение, при переключении A→B→A он не совпадает вообще никогда. Это значит на каждый клик:

- Rust читает **весь файл** аудио с диска и base64-кодирует его целиком,
- гигантская строка едет через IPC,
- JS вручную декодирует base64 побайтово (`atob`/`charCodeAt` в цикле) в `Uint8Array`,
- создаётся новый Blob + object URL, старый ревокается.

И это происходит для обеих заметок при каждом переключении, хотя ничего в аудио не менялось. Плюс по мелочи: при каждом переключении заново дёргается полный скан всех заметок под `list_recordings` (сейчас с двумя заметками дёшево, но это лишний round-trip), и фоновый auto-queue цикл каждые 15с сканирует всё дерево независимо от выбора.

Самое дешёвое и эффективное исправление — сделать загрузку аудио ленивой (по явному клику "Play", а не автоматом при открытии заметки), либо кешировать уже загруженные blob'ы вместо перезагрузки. Хотите, чтобы я это исправил?

## 3. Массовая загрузка существующих аудиофайлов (Voice Memos)

Сейчас такого пути нет — `save_audio_recording` принимает только base64 из браузерного `MediaRecorder`, готового пути к файлу на диске он не берёт. Ближайший аналог в кодовой базе — импортёр Apple Notes (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/import.rs`): та же архитектура (воркер-поток + global snapshot, который фронт поллит) отлично подходит и для аудио, только вместо парсинга текста — копирование файла.

Также нигде в коде нет мультивыбора файлов в диалоге (`open({ multiple: true })` нигде не используется, везде `multiple: false`) — Tauri это умеет, просто пока не задействовано.

Реализация — на самом деле умеренная по объёму: новая команда (либо переиспользовать `save_audio_recording` в цикле по файлам — проще, но повторяет base64-round-trip для каждого файла; либо новая команда с прямым `fs::copy` на стороне Rust — чище для больших/многих файлов), плюс новый пикер с `multiple: true` и фильтром по расширениям (m4a/wav/mp3 и т.п.), плюс цикл создания заметки на файл с постановкой в очередь на транскрайб (как уже делает рекордер после записи).

Хотите, чтобы я начал с чего-то из этого — например, сначала пофиксил лаги (пункт 2, самое конкретное и быстрое), а прогресс-бар и bulk-импорт оформил как отдельные задачи?

content.text:
**Что значит "блокирующий" здесь:**

Rust-код в `whisper.rs` запускает Python-скрипт через `Command::new(python).arg(&script_path)....output()`. Метод `.output()` — это вызов, который:
1. Стартует дочерний процесс,
2. **ждёт (блокирует текущий поток), пока процесс не завершится полностью**,
3. только после завершения получает весь `stdout`/`stderr` целиком одним куском.

То есть пока Python транскрайбит аудио (может занимать десятки секунд/минуты), Rust-поток просто спит на этом вызове и не имеет доступа ни к какой промежуточной информации — ни к тому, сколько сегментов уже обработано, ни к проценту выполнения. Он узнаёт "готово" только в момент, когда процесс уже завершился и вернул весь JSON разом. Это и есть "opaque blocking call" — с точки зрения Rust это чёрный ящик, который либо ещё не закончил, либо уже полностью закончил, ничего между.

Чтобы стримить прогресс, вместо `.output()` нужен `.spawn()` с `Stdio::piped()` для stdout, и построчное чтение через `BufReader` **пока процесс ещё работает** — тогда каждая строка (напечатанная Python-скриптом по мере обработки сегментов) видна сразу, а не в конце.

---

Понял по всем трём пунктам — везде делаем нормально, не срезаем углы. Это довольно объёмная работа, затрагивающая Rust-ядро, Tauri-команды и фронтенд в нескольких местах. Прежде чем писать код, хочу разложить архитектуру по каждой из трёх задач и согласовать план — особенно там, где есть развилки (например, как правильно отдавать аудио в плеер вместо base64-IPC, и как определять "дату создания" для импортированных файлов).

# Local Whisper Streaming Progress — Architecture Research

## 1. Current end-to-end data flow (Python exit → queue state → command → frontend poll → UI)

**Hop 1 — Python subprocess runs to completion, then exits.**
`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper.rs:136-146` — `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` calls `Command::new(python).arg(&script_path).arg(audio_path_str).arg(model).output()`. `.output()` blocks the calling thread until the child process exits and buffers all of stdout/stderr into memory — there is no incremental read of stdout while the process runs. The script itself (`whisper_scripts/transcribe.py:1-32`) does a single `json.dump(result, sys.stdout, ...)` **after** the `for segment in segments` loop fully completes (line 12-21, then line 30) — i.e. nothing is printed until transcription is 100% done. Progress on stderr doesn't exist either; only two `eprintln!` diagnostic lines wrap the call in Rust (`whisper.rs:131-134`, `161-165`), not the Python process.

**Hop 2 — Rust parses the single JSON blob.**
`whisper.rs:148-155` — parses `stdout` into `WhisperScriptOutput { text, language, language_probability, duration, words }` once, only after `output.status.success()`.

**Hop 3 — Worker thread updates the note's front-matter status synchronously.**
`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:611-707` (`process_transcription_job`): marks `RECORDING_STATUS_PROCESSING` at job start (line 612-618) with no intermediate updates, then on the `LocalWhisper` branch (line 626-632) calls `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` synchronously (blocks until subprocess exits), then writes `RECORDING_STATUS_COMPLETED`/`RECORDING_STATUS_FAILED` at the end (line 680-705) via `update_recording_note_status` (mod.rs:583-607), which rewrites the note's YAML front-matter on disk (`transcription_status`, `transcription_error`, `transcription_updated_ms`, `transcription_id`) — this is the persistence layer; there is no separate DB.

This job runs inside the queue worker loop `spawn_transcription_worker_if_needed` (mod.rs:710-751), on a plain `std::thread::spawn` (line 724) — see §3.

**Hop 4 — In-memory queue snapshot (separate from note front-matter) tracks queue-level state.**
`TranscriptionQueueState` (mod.rs:410-416): `running: bool`, `current_recording: Option<String>`, `pending: VecDeque<QueuedTranscriptionJob>`, `known_recordings: HashSet<String>` — held in a process-global `static TRANSCRIPTION_QUEUE: OnceLock<Mutex<TranscriptionQueueState>>` (mod.rs:420). `recording_queue_snapshot()` (mod.rs:442-456) builds `RecordingQueueSnapshot { running, current_recording, pending: Vec<String>, in_flight }` from it. Note: **this snapshot has no per-job progress field at all** — it only tells you *which* note is "current," not how far along it is.

**Hop 5 — `list()` merges queue snapshot + per-note status from disk.**
`RecordingsAdapter::list` (mod.rs:339-377) calls `recording_queue_snapshot()` (line 341) and `collect_recording_notes(&root)` (line 348, which re-reads every note's front-matter status from disk — mod.rs:564-580), builds `RecordingListItem` per note (`is_queued`/`is_processing` derived from queue membership, `status`/`error`/`updated_ms` from front-matter), returns `RecordingsListResult { queue, recordings }` (mod.rs:376).

**Hop 6 — Tauri command exposes `list()`.**
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs:68-72` — `#[tauri::command] list_recordings(app) -> Result<RecordingsListResult, String>` calls `recordings_use_cases(app)?.list()`. This is a **synchronous** (non-`async`) Tauri command, so Tauri runs it on its own command threadpool, not the main/UI thread — blocking inside it is fine (see §3). There's also `check_whisper_status` (commands/recordings.rs:53-66) and `queue_local_transcriptions` (36-42), `retrigger_transcription` (44-51).

**Hop 7 — Frontend polls on a timer, no push/events.**
`apps/desktop/src/features/recording/hooks/recordings-context.tsx:89-109` — `loadRecordingsSnapshot` calls `api.listRecordings()` and feeds `useProcessingQueue` (`apps/desktop/src/features/processing/hooks/use-processing-queue.ts:22-72`), which just does `loadSnapshot()` inside `refresh()` (no interval itself — needs to be called repeatedly by the consumer). The actual interval timer lives in the settings section: `apps/desktop/src/features/settings/components/desktop/transcription-section.tsx:126-136` — `hasActiveWork` is true when `queue.in_flight > 0` or any item `is_queued`/`is_processing`, and while true a `window.setInterval(() => void refreshRecordings(), 2500)` polls every 2.5s. There is also a background "scan for more work" loop unrelated to per-job progress: `apps/desktop/src/features/processing/hooks/use-auto-queue-loop.ts:14-41`, wired in `recordings-context.tsx:250-258` with `intervalMs` defaulting to 15000ms.

**Hop 8 — UI render.**
`transcription-section.tsx:19-31` derives `DisplayStatus` from `formatRecordingStatus(item)` (5 states: completed/processing/queued/pending/failed — mod.rs's `RECORDING_STATUS_*` constants, `lib.rs:80-84`); `processing` shows label `"Transcribing…"` with a pulsing dot (line 42-46) but **no percentage, no ETA, no segment text** — because none of that data exists anywhere in the pipeline today.

**Bottom line: there is currently zero incremental signal anywhere in this chain.** The subprocess buffers, Rust blocks on `.output()`, the queue snapshot has no progress field, and the frontend just shows a static "Transcribing…" spinner while polling every 2.5s.

## 2. What `model.transcribe()` returns / per-segment fields / duration availability

From `whisper_scripts/transcribe.py:9`: `segments, info = model.transcribe(audio_path, word_timestamps=True)`.

- faster-whisper's `transcribe()` API (used exactly this way here) returns a **tuple** `(segments, info)` where `info` (a `TranscriptionInfo`) is computed eagerly — language detection + total audio duration are resolved **before** any segment is yielded — while `segments` is a **lazy generator**: each `Segment` is decoded and yielded one at a time as the loop consumes it (`transcribe.py:15` `for segment in segments:`).
- Confirmed by the script itself: `info.language`, `info.language_probability`, `info.duration` are read at lines 24-27, and duration/language do not depend on having iterated any segments — this is the whole point of the `info` object's design in faster-whisper (VAD + duration are known from decoding the container/running VAD before the decode loop starts).
- Per-segment fields actually used: `segment.text` (line 16), `segment.words` (line 17) when `word_timestamps=True`; each word has `.word`, `.start`, `.end`, `.probability` (lines 18-22). Note the script **does not currently capture `segment.start` / `segment.end`** (only word-level timestamps), though faster-whisper `Segment` objects have `.start`/`.end` attributes available for the taking.
- **Conclusion: total audio duration (`info.duration`) is knowable up front**, before consuming any segments — this is exactly the fact needed to compute a `processed_seconds / total_duration` progress fraction as segments stream in, e.g. by printing each segment (or word) as NDJSON to stdout the moment it's yielded, computing `segment.end / info.duration`.

Once `protocol-asset` is enabled and the app is rebuilt, `core:asset:scope`-style permissions become available and must be added to a capability file (or `app.security.assetProtocol.scope` used instead/together, per Tauri v2's dual config surface — capability `fs`/`asset` scope entries and the top-level `assetProtocol.scope` glob list are the two knobs to check when implementing).

**The scope problem (dynamic per-profile root)**: `notes_root` is fully user-configurable to *any* absolute path chosen at runtime — confirmed at `crates/type-core/src/adapters/profiles/state.rs:497-533` (`normalize_notes_root_path`, `set_profile_notes_root_state`) and wired from the frontend via `set_profile_notes_root` (`apps/desktop/src/features/profiles/api/profiles-api.ts:50-53`). `notes_root()` itself (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/notes/mod.rs:64-78`) reads `active.notes_root` from persisted profile state — it is not confined to `app_data_dir`. Static glob scope entries in `tauri.conf.json`/capabilities files are evaluated at build/startup and can't predict a path the user picks later via a folder dialog. Caveats to plan around:
  - Tauri v2 does support **runtime scope mutation** for the fs/asset scopes (`@tauri-apps/plugin-fs`'s scope APIs, or by granting a broad-enough static pattern e.g. `**/Recordings/**` combined with validating the resolved path server-side before ever handing a `convertFileSrc` URL to the renderer — since this app already fully re-validates paths via `is_recording_audio_path_allowed` and `sanitize_relative`, the actual security boundary can stay in Rust rather than depending solely on Tauri's own scope glob).
  - A robust approach: keep static config permissive only for the notion of "any Recordings folder under any allowed root" is not expressible without knowing roots in advance; the realistic implementations are (a) update capability/asset scope at runtime when the profile switches (Tauri v2 exposes `Scope`/`asset_protocol` scope handles on the Rust side — `tauri::scope::fs::Scope` — that can be extended via `app.asset_protocol_scope().allow_directory(path, true)` or equivalent at profile-switch time), or (b) use a very broad OS-root glob (e.g. `$HOME/**`, `/**`) which works but is coarse-grained since scope in tauri.conf.json is otherwise static.
  - Platform notes: the asset protocol works on macOS/Linux/Windows uniformly once `protocol-asset` + config scope are set; the main OS-specific gotcha historically was Windows requiring `https://asset.localhost/` origin instead of `asset://localhost/` for CSP/protocol reasons, and macOS/Linux both use the custom scheme — worth verifying against the exact 2.10.x docs during implementation, but no code in this repo currently touches this at all so there's no existing workaround to preserve.

## 4. Existing direct-file-serving precedent — none

Checked the only other binary-attachment domain, handwriting/OCR images:
- `crates/type-core/src/adapters/handwriting/mod.rs` has `save_handwriting_attachment` but **no `read_attachment`/`read_image` command exists at all** — confirmed via `grep` for `read_.*attachment|AttachmentPayload|fn read_` returning nothing, and `apps/desktop/src/features/handwriting/api/handwriting-api.ts:1-40` only exports `saveHandwritingAttachment`, `queueHandwritingOcr`, `listHandwritingOcrJobs` — no read call.
- `apps/desktop/src/features/handwriting/components/handwriting-note-header.tsx` never renders an `<img>` or fetches the attachment bytes at all — it only shows OCR status text (`grep` for `img|src=|base64|Blob` in that file returns nothing).

So the recording audio base64 round-trip is the **only** file-serving path in the app today; there is no precedent to reuse, and no other UI surface would immediately benefit from/require the same change (though it's the same shape of problem for handwriting attachments if that ever needs a preview).

## 5. `note.audioPath` storage format — relative, needs resolution before `convertFileSrc`

- Written at save time as **root-relative**: `crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:264` — `meta.recording_audio_path = Some(strip_root(&root, &audio_path))`, and `strip_root` (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/notes/mod.rs:117-122`) strips the notes-root prefix and normalizes to forward slashes.
- Persisted in front matter as `recording_audio_path: <relative/path>` — parse/render in `crates/type-core/src/adapters/notes/front_matter.rs:77-79` (parse) and `:167-169` (render).
- Surfaced to the frontend as relative in three places: `RecordingWriteResult.audio_path` (`mod.rs:278`), `RecordingListItem.audio_path` (`mod.rs:360-363`), and note-preview's `recordingAudioPath` (`packages/shared/src/format.ts:216`, typed at `packages/shared/src/types.ts:22`).
- `read_audio` resolves it back to an absolute path server-side by joining onto `ensured_notes_root` (`mod.rs:380-382`): `root.join(sanitize_relative(&args.path)?)`.

**Consequence**: `convertFileSrc` needs an *absolute* filesystem path (see its own doc example in `core.d.ts:141-144`, joining `appDataDir()` + relative path first). Since `notes_root` is resolved only in Rust (profile-aware, not known to the frontend), the frontend cannot locally concatenate `notes_root + audioPath` to build an absolute path — there is currently no IPC command that exposes the active profile's absolute `notes_root` to the frontend at all (the closest is `activeProfile.notes_root` in `profiles-context.tsx:64`, which *is* already the absolute root string coming from backend profile state — confirmed same field name/shape as `crates/type-core/src/adapters/profiles/state.rs:161-176`, `:497`, `:533`). So the frontend already has the absolute root available via `useProfiles().activeProfile?.notes_root`, and joining `notes_root + "/" + audioPath` client-side (or, cleaner, adding a small Rust command that returns the already-resolved absolute path, reusing the same `sanitize_relative`/`is_recording_audio_path_allowed` validation as `read_audio` today) is the necessary extra step before calling `convertFileSrc`.</result>

input.prompt:
Design a concrete, file-level implementation plan for three related features in this Rust/Tauri + React desktop notes app (crates/type-core is the shared Rust core; apps/desktop is the Tauri+React frontend). Read AGENTS.md first. Do NOT write any code — this is plan design only, output a structured plan.

I already have thorough research (below) from three Explore agents. Use it as ground truth — don't re-derive, just design on top of it. Cite file:line from the research where relevant.

=== FEATURE 1: Real streaming progress for local Whisper transcription ===

Current state: `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` (crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper.rs:117-168) calls `Command::new(python)...output()` — fully blocking, single JSON blob returned only after the whole transcription finishes. The bundled `transcribe.py` script does `segments, info = model.transcribe(audio_path, word_timestamps=True)` then loops `for segment in segments` collecting everything into one dict, `json.dump`'d once at the end. faster-whisper's `info.duration` (total audio length) is known BEFORE any segments are consumed; `segments` is a lazy generator, so segment-by-segment progress is possible without changing the whisper model call itself — only the consumption/reporting needs to change.

The worker that ultimately calls this: `process_transcription_job` (crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs:611-707), invoked from a dedicated `std::thread::spawn` worker loop (`spawn_transcription_worker_if_needed`, mod.rs:710-751) — confirmed safe to block/loop synchronously here (not on an async runtime, not shared with Tauri's command dispatch).

Queue state today: `TranscriptionQueueState` (mod.rs:410-416: running/current_recording/pending/known_recordings) behind `static TRANSCRIPTION_QUEUE: OnceLock<Mutex<...>>` (mod.rs:420) — has NO per-job progress field. `RecordingQueueSnapshot` (mod.rs:101-106, the DTO returned to the frontend) similarly has no progress field. Frontend polls via `list_recordings` Tauri command (commands/recordings.rs:68-72) → `RecordingsAdapter::list` (mod.rs:339-377) → merges queue snapshot + per-note frontmatter status. Settings UI (`apps/desktop/src/features/settings/components/desktop/transcription-section.tsx:126-136`) polls every 2500ms via `window.setInterval` while `hasActiveWork` is true, and renders a static "Transcribing…" label with a pulsing dot (no percentage) at line 42-46.

Existing precedent for incremental progress snapshots to mirror: the Apple Notes importer (crates/type-core/src/adapters/import.rs) — `AppleImportState` struct (import.rs:134-152: running/done/total/processed/imported/skipped/failed/current/error/errors), global `OnceLock<Mutex<AppleImportState>>` (import.rs:156-159), a `with_state(|s| ...)` mutation helper (import.rs:186-190) called before/after each unit of work inside the worker loop (import_inner, import.rs:311-352), and a frontend poll hook (`apps/desktop/src/features/import/hooks/use-apple-import.ts`) at 250ms interval.

type-ffi (mobile) scope: confirmed local Whisper is desktop-only — `crates/type-ffi/src/recordings.rs` never references whisper.rs or LocalWhisper transcription method at all, so no mobile-side changes needed, though RecordingQueueSnapshot's DTO shape is mirrored in type-ffi for JSON consistency (type-ffi/src/recordings.rs:14-46) and should probably stay structurally in sync even if the new field is always None/unused on that path.

Design needed:
- Exact new field(s) on TranscriptionQueueState / RecordingQueueSnapshot (e.g. progress fraction 0.0-1.0, or processed_seconds+total_seconds) — recommend a concrete shape.
- Exact protocol change for transcribe.py: what it should print per segment (NDJSON line format), keeping the final full-result output compatible with today's `WhisperScriptOutput` parsing (whisper.rs:148-155) — i.e. design a wire format where intermediate lines are progress and a final line (or sentinel) is the full result, or some other clean split.
– How to correctly install progress lines into a swappable "current job progress" shared field: keep in mind this is a single OnceLock<Mutex> global; only one job is ever "current," matching the single-worker-thread design (mod.rs:711-723) — no per-job-id keying needed since there's only ever one job in flight.
- Exact change to whisper.rs: `.output()` → `.spawn()` with piped stdout, `BufReader::lines()` loop reading while process runs, updating shared state per line, keep stderr handling reasonable (still capture on failure for error messages).
- Exact change to process_transcription_job / worker to expose this to `recording_queue_snapshot()`.
- Exact frontend change: what new field(s) transcription-section.tsx should read and how to render (percentage bar? just augment the existing pulsing-dot label?). Recommend concrete UI treatment given existing component structure — keep changes minimal/consistent with existing Tailwind/shadcn styling patterns already there.
- Any risk/edge case: process crashes mid-stream (partial output, must not corrupt state); very short audio where progress goes 0→100 almost instantly; word-level vs segment-level granularity trade-off for progress line frequency.

=== FEATURE 2: Fix audio-loading architecture (replace base64 IPC round-trip) ===

User explicitly wants the "correct"/proper architecture, not a quick patch (e.g., not just "make loading lazy on click" — though that may still be part of the right design, it's not suficient alone).

Current flow (fully traced): note switch → useEffect in recording-note-header.tsx:88-96 (fires on every note-with-audio open since there's only one global "active audio" slot, so A→B→A never matches) → recordings-context.tsx:111-130 `playRecording` → `api.readRecordingAudio` → Tauri command `read_recording_audio` (commands/recordings.rs:74-81) → `RecordingsAdapter::read_audio` (mod.rs:379-394): `fs::read` ENTIRE file + base64-encode whole thing into one JSON string → frontend `fromBase64` manual byte-by-byte atob/charCodeAt loop (apps/desktop/src/shared/lib/notes.ts:19-26) → `new Blob(...)` → `URL.createObjectURL`.

Confirmed: recordings are NOT encrypted at rest (mod.rs:379-394 does plain fs::read, no crypto) — so serving the raw file directly via Tauri's asset protocol is not a security regression versus today.

Tauri asset protocol (`convertFileSrc`) is available in the installed @tauri-apps/api (2.10.1) but NOT currently wired up:
- Missing Cargo feature `protocol-asset` on the `tauri` dependency (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:24 currently only has `features = ["macos-private-api"]`).
- Missing `app.security.assetProtocol.enable`/`scope` block in tauri.conf.json (apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:25-27 currently just `{"csp": null}`).
- Missing `core:asset:*` permission grants in capabilities/default.json (apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:8-13).
- Scope challenge: notes_root is a fully dynamic, user-chosen absolute path per profile (confirmed via adapters/profiles/state.rs:497-533, set_profile_notes_root_state) — static glob scope config can't predict it ahead of time. Two real options: (a) grant a broad static scope (e.g. `$HOME/**` or similar) and rely on the ALREADY-EXISTING Rust-side path validation (`sanitize_relative`, `is_recording_audio_path_allowed`, mod.rs:522-525) as the real security boundary rather than Tauri's scope glob, or (b) mutate the asset-protocol scope at runtime when the active profile changes, using Tauri's `asset_protocol_scope()`/`Scope` handle to `allow_directory` the new root. Recommend which is more appropriate for a desktop notes app where notes_root is already fully trusted local user data (there's no untrusted multi-tenant boundary here — same trust level as the rest of the app's fs access).
- Path format: `note.audioPath`/`recording_audio_path` is stored ROOT-RELATIVE (mod.rs:264, `strip_root`), not absolute. `convertFileSrc` needs an absolute path. The frontend already has the active profile's absolute `notes_root` available via `useProfiles().activeProfile?.notes_root` (profiles-context.tsx:64) — but recommend instead adding a small new Tauri command that resolves+validates the relative audioPath server-side (reusing `sanitize_relative`/`is_recording_audio_path_allowed`, same validation as read_audio today) and returns the absolute path, rather than having the frontend concatenate root+relative itself (keeps the security check in Rust, avoids frontend needing to replicate path-joining/validation logic). Design this command's exact shape (e.g. `resolve_recording_audio_path(path: String) -> Result<String, String>`).
- No other file-serving precedent exists in the app (handwriting attachments have no read/display path at all currently) — this would be establishing the first pattern of its kind, so design it cleanly since it may be reused later.
- Design: exact new/changed files — Cargo.toml feature flag, tauri.conf.json assetProtocol block + scope, capabilities/default.json permission, new (or modified) Tauri command, and the frontend change to recordings-context.tsx/recording-note-header.tsx: replace `readRecordingAudio`+base64+Blob+ObjectURL entirely with `convertFileSrc(absolutePath)` fed directly as the `<audio src>`, eliminating the manual byte-decode loop, Blob creation, and object-URL lifecycle management entirely (the OS/webview handles range requests, streaming, and caching natively — this is what makes this the "correct" architecture: no full-file materialization in JS memory at all, works well even for large files, and lets multiple notes' audio remain trivially "loaded" simultaneously without the single-active-slot lag problem from before). Confirm whether `activeAudioPath`/`activeAudioSrc` single-slot state in recordings-context.tsx becomes entirely unnecessary once each note's `<audio>` element can just point directly at its own resolved asset:// URL (i.e. no shared "active audio" concept needed anymore — every RecordingNoteHeader can independently resolve+render its own player). This would also fully eliminate the original "laggy switching" bug at the root, since there's no more IPC-blocking-file-read on every switch.
- Also verify/flag: does the `read_recording_audio` Tauri command (base64 path) still need to be kept for the mobile/type-ffi path (mobile has no Tauri asset protocol, so type-ffi's `read_recording_audio` — used by React Native — must NOT be touched/removed; this fix is desktop-app-shell-only, i.e. only `apps/desktop-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs` + frontend, core adapter's `read_audio`/`ReadRecordingAudioArgs` should likely remain as-is for FFI/mobile compatibility unless it's cleanly separable).

=== FEATURE 3: Bulk audio file import (e.g. iPhone Voice Memos already exported to disk) with preserved created-date ===

User wants: pick one or more existing audio files from disk in Settings, import each as its own note, each note's created date = the SOURCE FILE's actual creation date (not import time).

Confirmed current gaps: `SaveRecordingArgs` (mod.rs:46-52) has no `created_ms` override — `RecordingsAdapter::save` (mod.rs:241-280) hardcodes `now_ms()` for both frontmatter `created_ms`/`updated_ms` (lines 259-269) AND (via `recording_note_file_name`→`allocate_note_file_name`) the filename's timestamp prefix (line 254, 257) — same `now` value feeds both, by construction, today.

`write_note_with_front_matter` (adapters/notes/front_matter.rs:222-230) is fully agnostic to "now" — it writes whatever `NoteFrontMatter.created_ms` the caller supplies. Proven by Apple import (`import_one`, import.rs:393-399) which sets `meta.created_ms = Some(parsed.created_ms)` from a non-"now" source already. So the write path is ready; only `RecordingsAdapter::save`'s hardcoding needs to change (add an optional override, defaulting to `now_ms()` when absent, so the live-recording flow via `save_audio_recording` is unaffected).

`allocate_note_file_name` (adapters/notes/naming.rs:155-176, via `utc_note_filename_timestamp`, naming.rs:29-40) already takes `timestamp_ms: i64` as a plain parameter for the UtcTimestampSlug branch — NOT hardwired to now anywhere in naming.rs itself. Only the call site (`recording_note_file_name`, mod.rs:916-931) needs to receive the real source-file timestamp instead of `now_ms()`.

Date-extraction pattern to reuse verbatim (Apple import's `file_created_ms`, import.rs:580-585):
```rust
fn file_created_ms(path: &Path) -> Option<i64> {
    let meta = fs::metadata(path).ok()?;
    let time = meta.created().or_else(|_| meta.modified()).ok()?;
    time_to_ms(time)
}
```
No OS-specific cfg-gating exists or is needed anywhere in the codebase for this — `.created()` failing (e.g. some Linux filesystems lack birthtime) already falls back to `.modified()` generically, confirmed as the only precedent (import.rs:583, notes/mod.rs:181). Since audio files have no frontmatter to read a date from (unlike Apple import's markdown/HTML source files), THIS filesystem-metadata step becomes the PRIMARY source (skip the frontmatter-parsing step from Apple import entirely; only the filesystem-metadata + now_ms-fallback tail of that waterfall applies).

Worker/progress pattern to mirror 1:1 (Apple import, import.rs): `AppleImportState`-shaped struct (running/done/total/processed/imported/failed/current/errors), `OnceLock<Mutex<...>>` global, `begin_*`/`with_state`/`*_snapshot` trio of functions, `ImportGateway::start()`'s approach of resolving notes_root BEFORE spawning the thread (so the worker only touches plain paths/args, never AppHandle — import.rs:20-23 comment explains why), `std::thread::spawn` worker, frontend poll hook at some interval (Apple import uses 250ms, `use-apple-import.ts`).

Order-file handling: `update_order_append(dir, names, is_folder)` (adapters/notes/tree.rs:294-311) must be called after each new note UNLESS target folder is Feed (guarded exactly this way at both existing call sites: recordings/mod.rs:271-273 and import.rs:400-402) — per AGENTS.md, Feed doesn't keep `.notes-order.json`.

Command/layering pattern to follow: Tauri commands in commands/recordings.rs and commands/import.rs are synchronous (non-async) `#[tauri::command]` fns, each doing `ensure_security_unlocked_for_app(...)` then `<domain>_use_cases(app)?.<method>(args)` — application-service facades (RecordingsUseCases/ImportUseCases) are pure pass-through wrappers over gateway traits (ports/recordings.rs, ports/import.rs), with all real logic in the adapters (RecordingsAdapter/ImportAdapter). A new command should follow this exact shape.

Recommended architecture (from research, already vetted): a NEW Rust-side command/adapter function (not a frontend loop over the existing `save_audio_recording`+base64 command) that takes an array of absolute source file paths + target folder + file-name-format, does direct `fs::copy`/`fs::read`+`fs::write` (no base64 anywhere, unlike the live-recording flow which must use base64 because its source is an in-browser blob) into `Recordings/` via `recording_audio_file_path`, extracts real timestamp via `file_created_ms`-style logic, builds NoteFrontMatter with that timestamp for both created_ms/updated_ms AND the filename prefix, writes via `write_note_with_front_matter`, appends to order file unless Feed. Whether this lives as new functions inside `adapters/recordings/mod.rs` (same domain, reusing RECORDINGS_STORAGE_FOLDER/recording_audio_file_path/RECORDING_FRONTMATTER_TYPE constants already there) or as a new sibling adapter module — recommend which, given it's clearly the "recordings" domain (audio → note), not really "import" (which is about Apple's specific text-note format).

Picker: no multi-file precedent exists yet in the frontend (all 3 existing `open(...)` calls use `multiple: false`, `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`) — need `open({ multiple: true, directory: false, filters: [{name: "Audio", extensions: [...]}], title: "..." })`, and note the return type becomes `string[] | null` instead of `string | null`, requiring an `Array.isArray` branch where existing call sites check `typeof selected === "string"`.

Design needed:
- Exact new Rust types/functions (SaveRecordingArgs-sibling struct for bulk import args, e.g. `ImportAudioFilesArgs { source_paths: Vec<String>, target_folder: Option<String>, file_name_format: ... }`), where they live (adapters/recordings/mod.rs vs new file), the new global state struct + OnceLock, the new Tauri command(s) (e.g. `import_audio_files` + `audio_import_status`), and how `RecordingsAdapter::save`'s created_ms hardcoding gets refactored to accept an optional override without touching the live-recording call site's behavior.
- Exact frontend design: new picker function in the recordings (or settings) feature's api layer, a new hook mirroring use-apple-import.ts's polling shape, and where in Settings UI this should be surfaced (recommend: likely near the existing Transcription section or a new "Import audio" subsection — check apps/desktop/src/features/settings/components/desktop/ for the existing sections list/registry, e.g. `lib/sections` per AGENTS.md, to slot in correctly) — note: should support both single- and multi-file selection per user's explicit request ("хочу как один загрузить так и несколько" = "want to be able to upload one as well as several").
- After copying+creating notes, they should feed into the SAME existing transcription queue as normal recordings (queue_local_transcriptions / the auto-queue loop) so they get transcribed automatically — confirm this "just works" once notes exist with the right frontmatter fields (transcription_status=pending, recording_audio_path set), or if anything extra is needed.
- Any risk/edge case: duplicate/collision filenames when importing many files at once (recording_audio_file_path already uses fresh UUID filenames per mod.rs:934-949, so no collision risk there); very large batch (dozens of files) — is fs::copy on a std::thread::spawn worker adequate (yes, matches Apple import's approach, no async needed); unsupported audio containers/extensions (should we validate extension client-side in the picker filter, and is that sufficient, or should Rust also sanity-check the file readable before proceeding).

=== OUTPUT FORMAT ===

For each of the 3 features, give:
1. A short summary of the chosen design (2-4 sentences).
2. A concrete list of files to create/modify with what changes to each (function signatures, struct fields, no full code — this is a plan, not an implementation).
3. Sequencing/dependencies between the 3 features if any (I don't think there are hard dependencies between them, confirm this or flag if there are).
4. Key open questions or decisions that should be confirmed with the user before implementation starts (e.g., the asset-protocol scope strategy choice, the exact progress-bar visual treatment, where bulk-import UI should live in Settings).

Be concrete and reference exact file paths / existing symbol names throughout. This plan will be written to a plan file and shown to the user for approval before any code is written.

# Implementation Plan: Whisper Progress, Native Audio Playback, Bulk Audio Import

## Feature 1: Real streaming progress for local Whisper transcription

### Summary

Convert `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` from `Command::output()` (blocking, single JSON blob) to `Command::spawn()` with piped stdout consumed line-by-line via `BufReader::lines()`. `transcribe.py` is changed to emit one NDJSON progress line per segment (plus one initial line carrying `total_seconds` before any segment is consumed) and a final tagged result line. A new `current_progress: Option<TranscriptionProgress>` field is threaded through `TranscriptionQueueState` → `RecordingQueueSnapshot`, updated via a callback wired in `process_transcription_job` (mod.rs) so `whisper.rs` stays free of queue-state knowledge — matching the existing layering where mod.rs owns the queue and `whisper.rs` is just a backend. Frontend renders a percentage/progress bar in both the Settings Transcription page and the per-note recording header.

### Files to create/modify

**`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper_scripts/transcribe.py`** (whisper.rs:14 embeds this)
- After `segments, info = model.transcribe(...)`, before consuming any segment, print an initial progress line with `total_seconds = round(info.duration, 3)` and `processed_seconds = 0.0`, flush stdout.
- In the `for segment in segments:` loop (currently transcribe.py:14-23), after processing each segment, print a progress line `{"type": "progress", "processed_seconds": round(segment.end, 3), "total_seconds": duration}` and flush (`sys.stdout.flush()` or `print(..., flush=True)`) so the parent sees it immediately rather than buffered.
- Change the final `result` dict (transcribe.py:25-31) to include `"type": "result"` and keep all existing fields (`text`, `language`, `language_probability`, `duration`, `words`) unchanged — this keeps `WhisperScriptOutput`'s existing fields deserializable as today, just with one added tag key.
- Rationale for segment-level (not word-level) granularity: segments are already several seconds each on typical audio, giving meaningful update frequency without flooding the pipe; word-level would require flushing on every word (much higher volume for negligible UX gain given the UI polls at 2500ms/6000ms anyway).

**`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper.rs`**
- Add `#[derive(Deserialize)] struct WhisperProgressLine { processed_seconds: f64, total_seconds: f64 }` and keep `WhisperScriptOutput` (whisper.rs:22-33) but add `#[serde(default)] r#type: Option<String>` is unnecessary — parse each line as `serde_json::Value` first, branch on `value.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str)`.
- Change `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` signature (whisper.rs:117-121) to accept a progress callback: `pub fn transcribe_audio_local_whisper(audio_path: &Path, model: &str, python: &Path, mut on_progress: impl FnMut(f64, f64)) -> Result<(String, String), String>`.

## Feature 2: Fix audio-loading architecture (Tauri asset protocol, no base64 round-trip)

### Summary

Replace the base64 IPC round-trip (`read_recording_audio` → `fs::read` whole file → base64 → frontend `atob`/`Blob`/`ObjectURL`) with Tauri's asset protocol (`convertFileSrc`) fed directly into `<audio src>`. A new desktop-only Tauri command resolves + validates a root-relative `audioPath` into an absolute path server-side (reusing the exact validation `read_audio` already does), so the frontend never replicates path-joining/security logic. Recordings are confirmed unencrypted at rest (mod.rs:379-394 plain `fs::read`), so this is not a security regression. The existing single "active audio" slot in `recordings-context.tsx` becomes unnecessary — each `RecordingNoteHeader`/list row can independently resolve and render its own `<audio>` pointed at its own `asset://` URL, which also eliminates the original "laggy switching" bug at its root (no more IPC-blocking full-file read on every note switch).

### Design decision: static broad scope vs. runtime scope mutation

Recommend **(a) a broad static scope** (e.g. allow `$HOME/**`, or platform-equivalent broad roots) relying on the **already-existing Rust-side validation** (`sanitize_relative`, `is_recording_audio_path_allowed` — mod.rs:522-525) as the real security boundary, not Tauri's glob scope. Rationale: `notes_root` is fully dynamic per-profile (profiles/state.rs:497-533) and can change at runtime on profile switch; option (b) (mutating `asset_protocol_scope()` on every profile switch) adds a new stateful synchronization point that must be kept correct across profile-switch/rename/move flows, for a trust boundary that doesn't actually exist in this app (there is no untrusted multi-tenant boundary — `notes_root` is already fully trusted local user data, same trust level as every other filesystem access this app performs). This should still be explicitly confirmed with the user (see Open Questions) since it is a genuine architectural choice, not purely mechanical.

- Add `getAudioImportStatus(): Promise<AudioImportState>` → `invokeLogged("audio_import_status")`.

**New file: `apps/desktop/src/features/recording/hooks/use-audio-import.ts`**
- Mirror `use-apple-import.ts`'s state machine (`idle → picking → importing → done/error`, 250ms poll interval, `beginPolling`/`stopPolling`, resume-polling-on-mount-if-already-running) but simpler (no scan/preview step — audio files don't need a preview phase the way Apple Notes folders do, since there's no ambiguity about what will be created, one note per file).

**`apps/desktop/src/features/settings/components/desktop/transcription-section.tsx`** (recommended placement — see Open Questions)
- Add a new card "Import audio files" (same `cardClass`/section styling as `import-section.tsx`) with: pick button (single call, no separate "single" vs "multiple" UI — one button, native multi-select dialog), a target-folder field (optional, defaults to Feed like `save`'s existing fallback at mod.rs:964-965), a progress bar identical in structure to `import-section.tsx:158-163`, and an errors `<details>` block identical to `import-section.tsx:179-192`. Newly imported notes will appear in the existing "Recordings" list below (same section, mod.rs `list()` scans all recording notes unconditionally) once `refreshRecordings()` is called on completion — call it via the hook's `onImported` callback, same pattern as `useAppleImport({ onImported: () => void refreshTree() })` at `import-section.tsx:23`.

**`packages/shared/src/types.ts`** — add `AudioImportState`/`ImportAudioFilesArgs` TS mirror types (same shape as `AppleImportState`/`AppleImportArgs` in `import-api.ts:8-38`, minus the folder-scan-specific fields).

### "Just works" confirmation for auto-transcription queueing
Confirmed: once a note exists with `note_type = "audio_recording"`, `recording_audio_path` set, and `transcription_status = "pending"` (exactly what `import_one_audio_file` writes), it becomes indistinguishable from any other recording note to `collect_recording_notes` (mod.rs:564-580) and `queue_recordings_with_method` (mod.rs:781-861). The existing `useAutoQueueLoop` in `recordings-context.tsx:250-258` (which calls `queueRecordingTranscriptions("auto")` on its own timer, independent of this feature) will pick up newly-imported notes on its next tick with zero additional wiring.

### Risks / edge cases
- **Filename collisions**: none — `recording_audio_file_path` (mod.rs:934-949) always allocates a fresh UUID-based filename, regardless of the source file's original name.
- **Large batches (dozens of files)**: `fs::copy` on a single `std::thread::spawn` worker is adequate and matches Apple import's approach (which does the equivalent per-file `fs::read_to_string`/`write_note_with_front_matter` work in the same way) — no async needed, no batching/chunking required beyond the existing per-file progress-counter update.
- **Unsupported audio containers/extensions**: filter the picker dialog client-side (as shown above) as the primary UX guard — this is advisory only (a user can still bypass OS file-type filters). Recommend Rust-side also do a light sanity check before committing to a copy: verify the file exists, is a regular file, and is non-empty (same class of check `save`'s `audio_bytes.is_empty()` guard already does at mod.rs:244-246) — but do **not** attempt to validate the audio codec/container itself in Rust (no such validation exists anywhere in the app today, and faster-whisper/ffmpeg will simply fail transcription with a normal `transcription_error` if the file is bogus, which is an acceptable, already-existing failure path).
- **Extension derivation for the copied file**: unlike `save` (which derives extension from a MIME type passed by the browser recorder, via `audio_extension_from_mime`), bulk import has a real file with a real extension already — recommend reusing `source.extension()` directly (lowercased) rather than routing through the MIME-based helper, falling back to `"webm"` only if the source has no extension at all. This is a small deviation from `save`'s existing helper and should be called out explicitly in the diff/PR description since it's a new code path, not a reuse of `audio_extension_from_mime`.

---

## Sequencing / dependencies between the three features

**No hard dependencies — confirmed independent.** They touch non-overlapping call sites:
- Feature 1 touches `whisper.rs`, `process_transcription_job`, `TranscriptionQueueState`/`RecordingQueueSnapshot`, and two frontend display components.
- Feature 2 touches Tauri config/capabilities, a new resolver command, and `playRecording`/`<audio>` wiring in the frontend.
- Feature 3 touches `RecordingsAdapter::save` (refactored, but behavior-preserving) and adds new adapter functions/commands/UI, reusing `recording_audio_file_path`/`recording_note_file_name`/`write_note_with_front_matter` that Features 1 and 2 don't touch.

The only soft interaction: Feature 3's imported notes will immediately be visible in whatever UI Feature 1 and Feature 2 land in (the Transcription section's recordings list, and each note's audio player) — but this is additive, not a sequencing requirement. Suggested implementation order for lowest integration risk: **Feature 2 first** (smallest, most mechanical, and removes a real bug), then **Feature 1** (self-contained backend + two small frontend renders), then **Feature 3** (the most new surface area, benefits from Features 1/2 already being in place so imported recordings show live progress and play via the asset protocol from day one rather than the old base64 path).

---

## Key open questions to confirm before implementation

1. **Feature 2 — asset-protocol scope strategy**: confirm the recommended static broad scope (e.g. `$HOME/**`) relying on Rust-side validation, vs. runtime scope mutation on profile switch. Also confirm the exact scope glob is acceptable (Windows/Linux path equivalents of `$HOME` may need `$APPLOCALDATA/**` or similar additions depending on where profiles can be created — profiles/state.rs shows `notes_root` is fully user-chosen, so it could in principle live outside `$HOME` entirely; need to decide whether to scope even more broadly, e.g. no scope restriction beyond `enable: true` with a maximally permissive glob, given the Rust-side check is the real gate).
2. **Feature 2 — context refactor scope**: confirm Option A (fully remove the single-slot `activeAudioPath`/`activeAudioSrc` from `RecordingsContext`, giving each consumer its own local resolved-src state) vs. Option B (keep the context shape, just swap the internals of `playRecording`). Option A is the more "correct" architecture per the explicit ask but touches more files.
3. **Feature 1 — visual treatment**: confirm the recommended split (Tailwind progress bar in Settings' Transcription section; plain-text percentage in the per-note `RecordingNoteHeader` metric grid) rather than a uniform treatment everywhere.
4. **Feature 3 — where the bulk-import UI lives in Settings**: recommend a new card inside the existing `transcription-section.tsx` (since imported recordings immediately show up in that page's recordings list and it's already the desktop audio hub) rather than the existing (differently-scoped) `recordings-section.tsx`, which today is explicitly documented as "Mobile voice transcription and handwriting OCR settings" (recordings-section.tsx:38-41) and would be a confusing place to add a desktop-only feature. Confirm this placement, or whether the user would prefer a dedicated new `SettingsSectionId` (e.g. `"audio-import"`) as its own top-level Settings entry instead.
5. **Feature 3 — extension/codec validation depth**: confirm the recommended light sanity check (exists, is a file, non-empty) is sufficient, or whether the user wants a stricter pre-flight check (e.g. shelling out to ffprobe/attempting a decode) before committing to the copy — the latter would add a new dependency/complexity not currently present anywhere in the codebase.
6. **Feature 3 — shared `file_created_ms` helper**: confirm whether to promote the existing `import.rs:580-585` private function into a shared `pub(crate)` utility used by both `import.rs` and the new recordings code (small opportunistic dedup) or simply duplicate it as `import.rs` already assumes no OS-specific cfg-gating is needed.

---

### Critical Files for Implementation

- crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/mod.rs
- crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper.rs
- crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper_scripts/transcribe.py
- apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/recordings.rs
- apps/desktop/src/features/recording/hooks/recordings-context.tsx
- apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json
- crates/type-core/src/adapters/import.rs


- Exact new Rust types/functions (SaveRecordingArgs-sibling struct for bulk import args, e.g. `ImportAudioFilesArgs { source_paths: Vec<String>, target_folder: Option<String>, file_name_format: ... }`), where they live (adapters/recordings/mod.rs vs new file), the new global state struct + OnceLock, the new Tauri command(s) (e.g. `import_audio_files` + `audio_import_status`), and how `RecordingsAdapter::save`'s created_ms hardcoding gets refactored to accept an optional override without touching the live-recording call site's behavior.

- Any risk/edge case: duplicate/collision filenames when importing many files at once (recording_audio_file_path already uses fresh UUID filenames per mod.rs:934-949, so no collision risk there); very large batch (dozens of files) — is fs::copy on a std::thread::spawn worker adequate (yes, matches Apple import's approach, no async needed); unsupported audio containers/extensions (should we validate extension client-side in the picker filter, and is that sufficient, or should Rust also sanity-check the file readable before proceeding).

For each of the 3 features, give:
1. A short summary of the chosen design (2-4 sentences).
2. A concrete list of files to create/modify with what changes to each (function signatures, struct fields, no full code — this is a plan, not an implementation).

# Implementation Plan: Whisper Progress, Native Audio Playback, Bulk Audio Import

## Feature 1: Real streaming progress for local Whisper transcription

### Summary

Convert `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` from `Command::output()` (blocking, single JSON blob) to `Command::spawn()` with piped stdout consumed line-by-line via `BufReader::lines()`. `transcribe.py` is changed to emit one NDJSON progress line per segment (plus one initial line carrying `total_seconds` before any segment is consumed) and a final tagged result line. A new `current_progress: Option<TranscriptionProgress>` field is threaded through `TranscriptionQueueState` → `RecordingQueueSnapshot`, updated via a callback wired in `process_transcription_job` (mod.rs) so `whisper.rs` stays free of queue-state knowledge — matching the existing layering where mod.rs owns the queue and `whisper.rs` is just a backend. Frontend renders a percentage/progress bar in both the Settings Transcription page and the per-note recording header.

### Files to create/modify

**`crates/type-core/src/adapters/recordings/whisper_scripts/transcribe.py`** (whisper.rs:14 embeds this)
- After `segments, info = model.transcribe(...)`, before consuming any segment, print an initial progress line with `total_seconds = round(info.duration, 3)` and `processed_seconds = 0.0`, flush stdout.

## Feature 2: Fix audio-loading architecture (Tauri asset protocol, no base64 round-trip)

### Summary

Replace the base64 IPC round-trip (`read_recording_audio` → `fs::read` whole file → base64 → frontend `atob`/`Blob`/`ObjectURL`) with Tauri's asset protocol (`convertFileSrc`) fed directly into `<audio src>`. A new desktop-only Tauri command resolves + validates a root-relative `audioPath` into an absolute path server-side (reusing the exact validation `read_audio` already does), so the frontend never replicates path-joining/security logic. Recordings are confirmed unencrypted at rest (mod.rs:379-394 plain `fs::read`), so this is not a security regression. The existing single "active audio" slot in `recordings-context.tsx` becomes unnecessary — each `RecordingNoteHeader`/list row can independently resolve and render its own `<audio>` pointed at its own `asset://` URL, which also eliminates the original "laggy switching" bug at its root (no more IPC-blocking full-file read on every note switch).

### Design decision: static broad scope vs. runtime scope mutation

Recommend **(a) a broad static scope** (e.g. allow `$HOME/**`, or platform-equivalent broad roots) relying on the **already-existing Rust-side validation** (`sanitize_relative`, `is_recording_audio_path_allowed` — mod.rs:522-525) as the real security boundary, not Tauri's glob scope. Rationale: `notes_root` is fully dynamic per-profile (profiles/state.rs:497-533) and can change at runtime on profile switch; option (b) (mutating `asset_protocol_scope()` on every profile switch) adds a new stateful synchronization point that must be kept correct across profile-switch/rename/move flows, for a trust boundary that doesn't actually exist in this app (there is no untrusted multi-tenant boundary — `notes_root` is already fully trusted local user data, same trust level as every other filesystem access this app performs). This should still be explicitly confirmed with the user (see Open Questions) since it is a genuine architectural choice, not purely mechanical.
